sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Arun Kumar Bajpai
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Arun Kumar Bajpai, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 27 of 2019, under Sections 376 I.P.C., Police Station Ghazipur, District Fatehpur, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by about four months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

Even an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved Gulab Chandra vs State Of U.P. on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194896478/
1 after a delay of 16 days on 15.09.2018.

entities.text: Gulab Chandra vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further stated that the inordinate delay speaks volume of false implication.
Learned counsel has further argued that there is no medical corroboration of the said incident.
The victim is a married lady.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
6. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 03.12.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Gulab Chandra, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
